summary: Corrected the published route to the milestone-listing slug (invariant #1: the listing name is 'Disable SVG filters on plugins and iFrames', the old folder used the broader detail name), recorded a move migration so the old route 301-redirects, and upgraded the content from summary-only to a nine-dimension, implementation-sufficient reference sourced from the csswg-drafts PR #13846 text, the WPT svg/styling reftests, and both vendor standards-positions.

rubric.evidence: Every behavioral claim now traces to a linked primary source: the restriction scope (cross-origin/restricted iframes, web plugins) and the ancestor-effect fallback algorithm are the ChromeStatus summary's exact wording; the proposed normative sentence is quoted from the csswg-drafts PR #13846 diff (fetched via the GitHub API, PR open/unmerged at review time); the srcdoc-retains-filter and reload-as-sandbox/cross-origin-navigation transitions come from reading the actual WPT test + reference files, not from the summary. The old page's 'pixel-readback side-channel' framing was replaced with the PR's clickjacking framing (pixel manipulation of inaccessible frames), which is what the cited sources actually say. Runtime-tested 2026-07-26 on Headless Chromium 150.0.7871.114 (Arch Linux) with a dual-origin rig (same-origin / cross-origin / sandboxed iframes + a CSS blur() control, all under filter: url(#feGaussianBlur), served from localhost vs 127.0.0.1): the restriction was NOT active in this build — cross-origin and sandboxed frames rendered blurred identically to the same-origin control, while the blur() control also blurred. The page records this observation verbatim in caveats; the listing's 'Enabled by default' is kept as the sourced record of intent but is NOT confirmed by the only runtime evidence available. Re-verify on an official Chrome 150+ stable build.

Feature 5117170452398080 appears in the live milestone=150 listing under 'Enabled by default' with the name 'Disable SVG filters on plugins and iFrames', which slugifies (lib/chromestatus.ts slugify) to exactly this route. The old route used the detail-style name; corrected per CLAUDE.md invariant #1 with a move migration recorded in migrations.json.

Case B (no MDN coverage): MDN search and HEAD checks found no page for this behavior change, so gendn keeps a full reference. reference-contract.json declares 3 inventory items x 9 dimensions, all documented with selectors, semantic pre/code examples, and tabular compatibility including explicit unknowns (no BCD entry; Edge unverified; fallback algorithm not specified by the open PR; no recorded console signal). Independent review must still compare every claim against the sources — structural green is not factual proof.

The lede separates what is restricted (SVG reference filters) from what is not (CSS filter functions, opacity/transform/backdrop-filter), which the old page conflated by implying all SVG filters on the frame were 'blocked' without naming the fallback. Caveats section records the open PR, the backdrop-filter gap raised in PR review, and the listing-vs-detail status discrepancy ('Enabled by default' in the listing vs 'Proposed' status text in the detail record, accurate_as_of 2026-06-01).

Live example: the identity-matched showcase concept filter-comparison is embedded (HEAD-checked 200) alongside links to sandbox-filter-test, clickjacking-replay, and svg-filter-policy-tester, plus a computed-style probe snippet. Three further pre/code blocks in the behavior reference mirror the WPT cross-origin/sandbox test markup (iframe), the WPT plugin test pattern (embed), and the ancestor-effect fallback (non-SVG wrapper effects survive).

Per-item compat tables plus a rolled-up browser-support section. Chrome rows cite the API record (desktop/android/webview 150, all Blink platforms); Safari cites WebKit standards-position #654 verbatim ('disables SVG filters on plugins and cross-origin iframes, but allows them on same-origin iframes'); Firefox cites Mozilla standards-position #1395 ('currently allows SVG filters on all iframes/plugins'). BCD absence and the Edge row are explicit unknowns, not invented.

Every named source is directly linked: feature page + API record, PR #13846, Filter Effects 1 draft, HTML clickjacking section, crbug 476646486, WPT directory + 9 individual test/reference files, both vendor positions. No plain-text source labels remain (the old page's bare 'chromestatus feature summary' labels are all linked now).

Single main + single h1 (with <wbr> break hints), sequential h1 -> h2 -> h3, labelled tables with caption + scope, baseline-banner as role=note with aria-label. Tap targets are links in running prose/tables (house pattern).

Wide tables wrapped in .table-wrap with overflow-x auto and overflow-wrap anywhere on cells (guidance size-aware-styling); pre blocks scroll horizontally instead of forcing page overflow. Dual-viewport matrix run via deno task responsive --page ... --screenshots at 360x740/DPR3 and 1280x800, plus MCP verification at 390x844 and 1280x800; screenshots read before recording ok/ok in responsive-support.json.

Whether Chrome emits any devtools/console signal when a filter is skipped is not recorded in any cited source (explicit unknown in the errors dimensions) — verify on a live build and document if one exists.

backdrop-filter on an element in front of a restricted frame is a separate, unrestricted mechanism per PR review discussion; if the spec or Chromium closes that path, add it as a new inventory item rather than editing the existing assertions.

Runtime verification on Chromium 150.0.7871.114 (2026-07-26) FALSIFIED the restriction for this build: cross-origin and sandboxed iframes rendered through the SVG filter, blurred like the same-origin control. Possible explanations: early-milestone/Finch-gated distro build, or the behavior landing later in the 150 cycle. The page's caveats section carries this observation; an official Chrome 150+ stable build must re-verify before the behavior is relied on.
